nodes.summary: Defines the handle_restaurant_confirmation() stored function (TBD/pending activation) that processes manual restaurant prep-time confirmations, updates delivery_summary, and eagerly calls process_delivery() to advance the dispatch flow.

nodes.name: archive_process_delivery.sql
nodes.summary: Archived version of the process_delivery() pg_cron function — Step 2 of the delivery workflow — that manages delivery_detail record creation, vehicle-type timeout progression, and triggers an AFTER UPDATE trigger when delivery_summary status reaches 'timedout'.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a multi-CTE pattern (deliverySnapShot → timedout_orders → update_summary → to_insert → insert_details) and includes a companion trigger definition for delivery_summary_timedout_whook.

nodes.name: cleanupDeliveryOrder.sql
nodes.summary: Defines the cleanup_delivery_order() utility function that destructively deletes all records for a given order number from delivery_inflight, delivery_dispatch, delivery_detail, and delivery_summary in the correct foreign-key order.
nodes.languageNotes: Intended only for testing and maintenance; explicitly warns against production use without authorization.

nodes.name: dispatch_cancel_before_pickup.sql
nodes.summary: Defines dispatch_cancel_before_pickup() — the RPC function called by the rider agent tool when a rider declines an assigned delivery before pickup, safely rolling back dispatch state, deleting the inflight record, reopening all vehicle-type detail rows, and resetting the timeout clock via redispatch_dtts.
nodes.languageNotes: Sets redispatch_dtts = NOW() so process_delivery() uses COALESCE(redispatch_dtts, dtts) as the timeout base, granting the re-dispatch a full window.

nodes.name: dispatch_complete_func.sql
nodes.summary: Defines dispatch_complete_func() — Step 6 in the delivery workflow — that marks delivery_dispatch, delivery_detail, and delivery_summary as 'completed' and removes the delivery_inflight record for the given dispatch_id.
nodes.languageNotes: Also includes a standalone UPDATE snippet that times out unassigned dispatches older than 30 seconds, useful for maintenance SQL execution.

nodes.name: enquire_admin_availability.sql
nodes.summary: Defines enquire_admin_availability() which reads restaurant admin lists from restaurant_master, builds a JSON payload, and POSTs to the /delivery-hooks/admin-availability-enquiry endpoint using the pg_net http_post extension.
nodes.languageNotes: Accepts an optional VARCHAR[] filter to target specific restaurants; reads ORDELO_APP_URL from ordelo_config.

nodes.name: enquire_shift_availability.sql
nodes.summary: Defines enquire_shift_availability() which aggregates active riders from rider_master (up to 20) and POSTs the payload to the /delivery-hooks/shift-availability-enquiry endpoint, enabling the app to determine which riders are on-shift.
nodes.languageNotes: Reads ORDELO_APP_URL from ordelo_config; silently handles EXCEPTION to return false on failure.

nodes.name: init_delivery.sql
nodes.summary: Defines init_delivery() — Step 1 of the delivery workflow — which reads customer and restaurant master data plus a confirmation-code salt from ordelo_config, inserts the initial delivery_summary row with status 'restaurant_unconfirmed', and returns the full record.
nodes.languageNotes: Generates confirmation codes as complementary pair (rest + cust = salt) using floor(random(...)) arithmetic; RETURNS TABLE mirrors all delivery_summary columns for the RPC caller.

nodes.name: init_delivery_detail_tbd.sql
nodes.summary: Defines init_delivery_detail() (TBD/pending activation) which bootstraps a delivery_detail row for a given order by finding the rank-1 vehicle type from delivery_option and delegating insertion to insert_delivery_detail().

nodes.name: init_takeaway.sql
nodes.summary: Defines init_takeaway() which initialises a takeaway_summary record by reading restaurant_master and customer_master data, generating a restaurant confirmation code, and inserting the row with status 'restaurant_unconfirmed'.
nodes.languageNotes: Parallel to init_delivery() but for the takeaway flow; falls back to cust_id as customer name when customer record not found.

nodes.name: insert_delivery_detail.sql
nodes.summary: Defines insert_delivery_detail() which resolves restaurant, customer, and delivery-option data and inserts a fully populated delivery_detail row for a given order number and vehicle type.
nodes.languageNotes: Derives rest_ref from the order_number prefix (first hyphen-delimited segment); raises EXCEPTION if any of the three required lookups fails.

nodes.name: job_assign_dispatch.sql
nodes.summary: Defines job_assign_dispatch() and assign_accepted_dispatch() — Step 4 of the delivery workflow — using rank() OVER (PARTITION BY order_number ORDER BY dispatch_id ASC) for race-condition-safe first-accept-wins logic, updating dispatch/detail/summary tables and inserting into delivery_inflight to trigger the rider graph.
nodes.languageNotes: assign_accepted_dispatch uses a single multi-CTE transaction: acceptedDispatches → acceptedDispatch → updateDispatch → updateDetail → updateSummary → insertInflight; the rank() window function ensures only the earliest-accepted dispatch wins.

nodes.name: job_awsrunner_switch.sql
nodes.summary: Defines job_awsrunner_switch() which controls AWS App Runner services (elaib and ordelo) by making GET requests to a Supabase Edge Function to resume or pause both services atomically.
nodes.languageNotes: Validates the action parameter ('resume'|'pause') before making calls; uses http_get() for both services sequentially and returns composite success status.

nodes.name: job_close_thread.sql
nodes.summary: Defines job_close_thread() scheduled every 5 minutes, which identifies inactive non-retained threads in the thread table and POSTs them to /delivery-hooks/close-threads to trigger farewell messages and thread closure.
nodes.languageNotes: Reads THREAD_INACTIVE_TIME_INTERVAL and ORDELO_APP_URL from ordelo_config; only POSTs when at least one thread qualifies.

nodes.name: job_create_dispatch.sql
nodes.summary: Defines job_create_dispatch() and get_available_riders() — Step 3 of the delivery workflow — which fans out dispatch records to available riders using LATERAL join, respects DISPATCH_BATCH_SIZE_ config per vehicle type, and marks vehicle types as timed-out when no riders are available.
nodes.languageNotes: get_available_riders() excludes both riders already dispatched for the same order and riders currently in delivery_inflight (globally inflight), preventing double dispatch.

nodes.name: job_null_or_outdated_location.sql
nodes.summary: Defines job_null_or_outdated_location() which detects inflight deliveries with missing or stale rider location data and POSTs affected (order_number, rider_id) pairs to /location-hooks/null-or-outdated-location for remediation.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses LEFT JOIN between delivery_inflight and rider_location; distinguishes NO_LOCATION_DATA vs OUTDATED_LOCATION_DATA reasons; interval driven by LOCATION_ENABLE_TIME_INTERVAL config.

nodes.name: job_process_owntracks.sql
nodes.summary: Defines job_process_owntracks() (SECURITY DEFINER) which batch-reads up to 1000 messages from the pgmq 'owntracks' queue, splits them into location and transition events, inserts into rider_location and rider_location_event tables, and archives processed messages.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses pgmq.read() + pgmq.archive(); the multi-CTE pattern (msgs → parsed → location_rows/transition_rows → loc_insert/event_insert → msg_id_collect) runs all inserts in a single statement.

nodes.name: job_restaurant_confirmation_timeout.sql
nodes.summary: Defines job_restaurant_confirmation_timeout() scheduled typically every minute, which auto-transitions restaurant_unconfirmed orders to 'unassigned' after a restaurant-specific (or global fallback) timeout, defaulting prep time to 25 minutes to keep the dispatch flow moving.
nodes.languageNotes: Resolves timeout via COALESCE chain: {rest_ref}_RESTAURANT_CONFIRMATION_TIMEOUT → RESTAURANT_CONFIRMATION_TIMEOUT → 5 minutes hardcoded fallback.

nodes.name: job_terminate_stale_active_threads.sql
nodes.summary: Defines job_terminate_stale_active_threads() which fires a POST to the /thread-hooks/terminate-stale-active-threads FastAPI endpoint, delegating stale-thread detection logic to the application layer.
nodes.languageNotes: Unlike job_close_thread which does filtering in SQL, this function is a thin webhook dispatcher that passes an empty payload; all business logic resides in the FastAPI handler.

nodes.name: notify_missed_dispatches_tbd.sql
nodes.summary: Defines notify_missed_dispatches() and notify_missed_dispatches_for_order() (TBD) which detect accepted dispatches on already-assigned orders — indicating a race condition — and POST the anomaly data to /delivery-hooks/notify-missed-dispatches for alerting.
nodes.languageNotes: Identifies rows where delivery_dispatch.status='accepted' AND delivery_detail.status='assigned' for the same order, which signals a rider accepted after another rider was already assigned.

nodes.name: ordelo_post
nodes.summary: PostgreSQL helper function that performs HTTP POST requests to URLs constructed from ordelo_config entries, acting as a reusable wrapper over the pg_net/http_post extension for calling FastAPI webhook endpoints from SQL.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the pg_net/http extension (http_post) and reads base URLs from the ordelo_config table by config_key, enabling database-driven endpoint routing.

nodes.name: process_delivery
nodes.summary: Core pg_cron scheduled function (every 5 seconds) that drives delivery status transitions by inserting the next eligible vehicle-type delivery_detail row when prior ones time out, and marking delivery_summary as 'timedout' when all vehicle types are exhausted, using restaurant-specific or global timeout config from ordelo_config.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses CTEs chained with UNION ALL to atomically compute vehicle ranking, detect all-timed-out orders, and INSERT next delivery_detail in a single query pass. Timeout is measured from redispatch_dtts when present (re-dispatch support) or dtts otherwise.

nodes.name: process_restaurant_confirmation
nodes.summary: pg_cron scheduled function (every 5 seconds) that times out restaurant confirmations for both delivery_summary and takeaway_summary orders where restaurant_confirmation_status is 'restaurant_unconfirmed' or 'restaurant_accept' and no pickup_time has been set within the configured interval, transitioning them to 'restaurant_timedout' and triggering the delivery_hooks webhook.
nodes.languageNotes: Handles both delivery and takeaway order flows in a single function using UNION ALL over two UPDATE CTEs. Timeout value cascades: restaurant-specific config key, then global key, then 5-minute fallback.
